For example, predicting the next word from "Your neighbor's name is" is harder than predicting the next word from "To be or not".  For most people, this is indistinguishable from actual intelligence.  With enough optional paths, it may generate a vector of tokens which represent novel information, such as the counterexample values for the Navier-Stokes Fluid Dynamics equation, or a method for exploiting a vulnerability in a software system.  Calling this intelligence is laughable.

Adding more data to a pre-trained transformer is only going to change the weights for each token, so a token like "King" might have 64k embeddings instead of 16k, but these weights will change less with a single value as more values are considered.  Adding a new value to an average of 1000 values will only change the average slightly.  

For inference, the  length of the token input vector, called the "context window" provides more information against the weight matrix, but that creates more certainty for each token evaluation, so the model is less likely to consider alternate paths with more tokens.  In essence, these models apply confirmation bias which worsens with the length of the input token vector.  If there is a previous position in the vector where choosing a less immediately optimal token would generate a better overall fit given later text, an LLM won't find it, because it would require pursuing multiple paths, potentially exponentially.
